thread:
maria: alert from runtime: repeated CUDA OOMs on gpu-node-37 despite ~1.1GiB headroom reported by headroom-service. multiple pods failed with container crashloop. stack dump attached.

incident-bot: [ALERT] runtime.cuda.oom on gpu-node-37 · 1851234567 · Severity: P1 · count: 8 · linked: https://pager.redwood/INC-3982

kai (on-call): seeing same. paging logs now. root cause unknown. maria which model and batch sizes? any recent deploys?

maria: no deploys. model: redwood/gptx-13b-8bit, batch target 4, max_seq 2048. headroom-service reports 1.1GiB free when sampling.

adam: pinged infra for GPU-level metrics, pulling nvidia-smi and cgroup info.

leo: past incidents have been fragmentation + reserved-blocks causing ghost allocations. can we get allocator debug?

maria: pushing allocator logs now:

```
[2026-05-04T03:02:11Z] allocator: reserve(512MB) -> success
[2026-05-04T03:02:12Z] kv-cache: prefetch 200MB
[2026-05-04T03:02:13Z] runtime: attempt alloc 600MB -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-05-04T03:02:13Z] allocator: free_headroom reported 1.1GiB
[2026-05-04T03:02:13Z] allocator: fragmentation metric: free_chunks: 14, avg_chunk: 48MB, reserved_blocks: 6
```

kai: interesting — free_headroom measurement doesn't account for reserved blocks and fragmentation. we need immediate mitigation: drain new requests from gpu-node-37, set routing fallback.

jen (sre): temporarily re-routed traffic away from node pool "rt-gpu-37" and set concurrency cap to 1 for suspect pods. issuing kube drain for node.

```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-37
kubectl drain gpu-node-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
```

adam: evicting currently running pods caused a few graceful exits but some containers crash before termination due to oom on teardown. I'm forcing restart of runtime process on the node.

```
ssh root@gpu-node-37
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 --no-pager
```

infra-bot: GPU utilization snapshots and reserved-blocks histogram posted in #incidents.

maria: applied temporary runtime config tweak to disable kv-cache reservation and lower allocator reserved slab via admin API:

```
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8081/admin/config -d '{"kv_cache.reserve": false, "allocator.reserved_slab_mb": 256}'
# runtime returned 200
```

kai: that should reduce pre-reserved memory pressure. also reduced per-request max_batch to 2 on the routing layer to lower burst allocation.

leo: spun up fallback pool using redwood/gptx-6b-8bit and moved 30% of traffic there as graceful degradation for latency-sensitive customers.

jen: customer-impact report: 1 customer (acme-inc) saw 503s and 10% higher latency for 12m window. CS notified. no data leakage.

adam: after the drain + restart + config changes, runtime stopped producing OOMs on node-37. monitoring shows stable allocations and headroom now correlates with usable memory.

maria: will keep node cordoned until we roll the restart+patch across pool. plan: backfill node with test traffic and then uncordon.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] incident assigned to kai, severity P1 -> mitigated.

kai: quick postmortem notes: root cause is allocator/reservation mismatch — allocator's free_headroom was reporting logical free space but reserved_blocks + fragmentation blocked contiguous allocation for typical GPU kernels; kv-cache prefetching amplified reserved fragmentation. steps taken: 1) disable kv-cache reservation fallback 2) lower reserved slab 3) routing fallbacks to smaller model 4) node restart to release leaked reserved segments.

leo: proposed long-term fixes: allocator should report two headroom numbers (logical vs contiguous) and expose fragmentation. add aggressive coalescing on free and a background compaction pass. also add max-reserve-per-request throttles.

jen: opened follow-up tasks:
- infra: allocator compaction API (TICKET-512)
- runtime: add contiguous_headroom metric + dashboard (TICKET-513)
- devex: add fallback routing recipe to runbook (TICKET-514)

maria: I'm drafting a customer-impact email for acme-inc and internal postmortem. will include timeline and mitigations.

adam: handoff to SRE for watch: @jen you'll own next 2h, @kai will track allocator ticket and coordinate with infra.

jen: ack. I'll monitor and coordinate rolling restart across pool. leaving node cordoned until patch hits images. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks all — good mitigation work. will post final postmortem when available. :coffee:

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] incident marked mitigated at 1851235167. followups: TICKET-512, TICKET-513, TICKET-514
